reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap record tagged as a data center in Spain carries a name, "The Weaver," that gives no sign of any computing or hosting business, and its true identity is unconfirmed.

The record sits at latitude 38.2938412, longitude -0.5892208, 1.9 miles from Alicante-Elche Miguel Hernández Airport. It is tagged telecom=data_center and named The Weaver. The name points toward textiles, craft, or a hospitality or creative business rather than IT infrastructure. The research note states plainly that the tag may have been misapplied to an unrelated premises, and that this could not be confirmed because the search quota was exhausted.

For AI infrastructure, the relevant fact is that this entry contributes nothing to the count of real data-center capacity. A facility record with no operator, no website, and no confirmed function cannot be read as a building that houses servers, draws power, or supports compute. If such records are aggregated into maps of data-center density, they inflate the apparent footprint without adding a single megawatt.

What the data does not tell the reader is whether a genuine data center exists at these coordinates under a different name, or whether the tag is simply wrong. It also does not establish how many other records in the same dataset share this problem, only that the pattern is described as recurring. The honest reading is that this is one unverified point, not evidence about the Spanish data-center market or about grid load in Alicante.
